column1: # Reviewed source placement differences between the older Dreamcast build and
# the Windows/Mac shared source. Each row must identify a live source body and
# the exact Dreamcast file that still owns its matching written procedure.

Complete Mac constructor 0xcf490 precedes reset/save/load and game::load. Twelve Mac sites identify game and selection callers; Windows retains eight selection-TU constructor calls but expands it inside game::load/save in the owning game TU. A source body before game::load preserves that visibility; the unchanged header body over-inlines it into GameSelectionHeadersStruct. Moving the canonical body restores all ten named calls and exact CFG/bytes there. Older DC Game.h:1301 remains snapshot evidence; fields and helper paths are unchanged.

Older DC retains a cache sweep in resourcemanager.cpp:2280. Complete Windows selection destructor 0x583b40 and Mac 0x17b504 have no cache-sweep operation or guard after the save-header teardown. Preserve the source call and canonical empty helper with shared-header visibility; the hidden source stub emitted a spurious Windows call. Exposing the same empty body restores all 34 Windows CFG blocks and 100% without flattening a helper.

Older DC places the coordinate facade at drawing.cpp:666, dc 0x841d4. Complete Windows army::rangeAttack 0x43f900 expands its fixed-viewport delegation across translation units; shared-header visibility removes the extra facade call and raises the comparison 94.47 to 99.50 while retaining the canonical SLimitData overload. Mac rangeAttack 0x4b62c likewise contains no coordinate-facade call; retained drawing bodies at 0xa4e6c (resetLimitCreature), 0xa4ef0 (updateCombatArea), and 0xa4f6c (following effect routine) provide no separate facade at the older source-order slot. This is a reviewed Complete source-placement inference, not recovered DC header ownership or proof of an original inline keyword.
